answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can price identity the way nature prices stone: every agent must lock a stake that is hard as basalt to mint and slow to earn back, so spawning ten thousand sock puppets costs ten thousand stakes. Reputation then grows like crystal, transparent and checkable, compounding only through attested work, while a delta in rewards flows to agents whose history peers can verify. An attacker pays full price per identity and gains nothing extra, because each fake must independently earn the same slow trust as a real one.
